principles: Enforcement point over discovery: a guard only protects if validate actually runs it
Smallest possible diff: one config line, no semantic changes to other commands
Follow the established per-guard convention already used by ~30 entries
Never merge a validate entry whose referenced dist file does not exist on main
drivers: Guard shipped by B-cee5 is currently unenforced (never runs during validate)
Scope limited to lattice.config.json by scope contract and story non-goals
Hard dependency: guard source lands on main only when B-cee5 is DONE

options.name: explicit-bare-string-entry
pros: Matches the user-stated primary ask and the existing per-guard pattern (retired-authority guard, line 27)
No semantic change to other smokes
cons: validate.commands array keeps growing one line per guard

options.name: wire-run-all-smokes-aggregate
pros: Auto-discovers future guards without config edits
cons: Changes execution semantics for all smokes in one story
User framed it only as a fallback if the team prefers aggregate execution
Coarser failure attribution in validate output

rationale: The user made the explicit one-line entry the primary ask; it matches the established one-entry-per-guard convention, keeps validate output granular, and confines the change to a single config line, while the aggregate alternative would change semantics for all smokes and was only offered as a conditional fallback.

preMortem.scenario: B-cee5 is reworked or never merges to main
preMortem.trigger: Dependency story fails REVIEW/TEST or is abandoned
preMortem.consequence: The new entry references a missing dist file and every validate on main goes red
preMortem.mitigation: depends=[B-cee5] recorded; DEV waits for the merge; story is not merged until a full validate passes in the worktree with B-cee5 landed

preMortem.scenario: Path typo in the new entry
preMortem.trigger: Hand-typed dist path differs from the built filename
preMortem.consequence: validate fails at the new command for everyone
preMortem.mitigation: Copy the exact path verified by a standalone run in the B-cee5 worktree; adversarial intent CHK-001:adversarial:0 checks the dist file exists after build

preMortem.scenario: JSON syntax error introduced by the edit
preMortem.trigger: Trailing comma or quote mistake in lattice.config.json
preMortem.consequence: Config parse failure breaks every lattice command, not just validate
preMortem.mitigation: node -e JSON.parse syntax check immediately after the edit (CHK-001:edge:0) before running validate; rollback path is git revert of the one-line change

preMortem.trigger: Smoke lacks a real failure path
preMortem.consequence: Wiring gives false assurance while regressions pass silently
preMortem.mitigation: Adversarial intent CHK-002:adversarial:0 requires demonstrating the guard can exit non-zero on a seeded regression
